name: tidy
description: Cleans up Gmail and YouTube subscriptions with AI without letting AI loose on your account. A small model judges each email; plain, tested code decides what that judgment may do; nothing risky happens until you approve.
highlights: Never deletes, never touches starred mail, never clicks unsubscribe links

name: iphone-backup-linux
description: A Claude Code plugin that backs up an iPhone from Linux with no iTunes and no sudo: a full encrypted backup you can restore to any iPhone, plus a photo archive that only ever adds files, so photos survive being deleted from the phone.
highlights: First run: a 121 GB encrypted backup and 20,371 photos archived by month
Passed all 7 checks for Claude's plugin directory; in review there now

name: post-reviewer
description: Paste in a post, README or screenshot about a tool you're thinking of adopting and get a signal-or-noise verdict for your own setup: adopt, trial or skip, with every claim checked against the files and marked supported, unsupported, contradicted or unverifiable.
highlights: Tuned on 13 real cases, with Opus 5.5 grading Sonnet 5.5's reviews
Correct verdicts rose from 62% to 96%, and invented facts dropped by about two thirds

name: why-slow
description: An agent skill that finds out why a Linux machine feels slow: load, swap, RAM-backed /tmp, CPU heat and throttling, OOM kills and stuck processes, all read-only. Fixes happen one approved step at a time, and processes you protect, like tmux or other agent sessions, are never touched.
highlights: Its first run found a stuck image loader that had kept one core at 100% for 13 hours and cooled the CPU from 87 °C to 61 °C

name: claude-mods
description: Five Claude Code mods built from my own session logs: Claude read my last 20 sessions, found what I keep asking it, and turned the top asks into live UI. A line above the prompt says what's waiting on me and how much room my other account has; side panes show whether each repo is pushed, green and deployed, and what every parallel session is doing.
highlights: Built from real usage: 16 manual account switches and repeated "what's next?" asks across 20 sessions
Guards stop Chrome actions in the wrong profile and commands that would close my own session

name: ai-workbench
description: A Claude Code skill that sets up my Linux dev machines: one matrix-green and cyber-purple theme across prompt, terminal, editor and status line, plus T3 Code over Tailscale, always-on hosts, offline voice typing and remote desktop between machines. It reads your config before touching it.

name: awesome-copilot-toolkit
description: A VS Code extension to browse and install custom instructions, prompts and chat modes from the github/awesome-copilot repository without leaving the editor.

name: macify
description: Makes Ubuntu GNOME look like macOS in one command, with a one-command revert.

name: sponsor-check
description: Does this company sponsor work visas? Search the UK Home Office register of licensed sponsors and US H-1B approvals by company name, in a browser or from one standard-library Python file. Rebuilt daily from the official data.
highlights: 127,606 UK sponsors and 27,146 US H-1B employers, searchable on a phone
Feeds my job-search pipeline: a JD that says nothing about visas now gets checked against the register

name: explore-mullana
description: A free map and directory of shops and places in Mullana, a small town in Haryana, and around the MMDU university campus. Built in September 2026 to put my hometown on the map and help students and residents find local shops.
highlights: A 3D view of the town's 4,877 buildings, drawn from open Overture Maps footprints
Open-now filter, nearest-first sorting, and call, WhatsApp and directions on every shop
Shops are listed through a Google Form; nothing is published without the owner's consent and an approval step
Runs at $0 on Cloudflare Pages, Pages Functions and KV

name: mullana-committee-tracker
description: A shared ledger for a monthly savings group run among friends: who has paid in, by cash or UPI, and a running record for every month. Members sign in with Google to check the group's status from their phones.
highlights: All the payout and dues maths lives in one tested function

name: led-catalog
description: A catalog of LED display programs for Bansal Lights Decorator, my father's lighting business in Mullana. Technicians keep each controller program with a photo and notes in English and Hindi, offline in the browser, and write it to an SD card from desktop Chrome or Edge.
highlights: Writes the program to the SD card, then reads it back and checks the copy byte for byte

name: home-list
description: A shared chores list for two people in one home, installed on both phones as a home-screen app. Tasks can have a complete-by time; each phone gets a push when the other person adds a task, and a reminder an hour before one is due. Invite-only: only allowlisted Google accounts can see the list.
highlights: Reminders every five minutes at no cost: a Cloudflare Worker cron calls the app, because Vercel's free cron runs only once a day

name: expense-tracker
description: A shared expense tracker for housemates: quick entry, filters by category, type and date, and monthly summaries with the net position and a category breakdown. Changes show up live for everyone signed in with Google.
highlights: Real-time sync and Google sign-in come from Convex, so there is no server to run
